=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Links.md === # FEATURE: Links | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261014 V1 | | Description | Implement the look-for-link-or-image procedure and the inline, full, collapsed and shortcut link forms with the destination and title grammar. | | Depends On | FEATURE-Emphasis.md, FEATURE-Link-Reference-Definitions.md | | Provides | look_for_link_or_image procedure, link destination and title grammar | | Consumes | delimiter stack, process_emphasis procedure, reference map, normalize_label | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Implement the Links section of the spec following the Appendix "look for link or image" procedure. The `![` machinery is shared with images; image rendering belongs to the images story. ## Procedure - On `]`, search the delimiter stack from the top for a `[` or `![` opener. If none is found, emit literal `]`. If the opener is inactive, remove it and emit literal `]`. - Otherwise parse ahead for, in order: an inline link `(`destination, title`)`; a full reference `[label]`; a collapsed reference `[]`; a shortcut reference. References resolve through `normalize_label` and the reference map. A full reference whose label is not defined falls back to the shortcut form of the link text only if it is not followed by a label. - On success, build the link node from the inlines after the opener, run `process_emphasis` with the opener as `stack_bottom`, and remove the opener. For a link (not an image), set every earlier `[` opener inactive, so links never nest. - On failure, remove the opener and emit literal `]`. ## Grammar - A destination is `<...>` with no line ending and no unescaped `<` or `>`, or a nonempty run with no space or control characters and balanced unescaped parentheses (at least three levels). An empty destination is allowed. - A title is double-quoted, single-quoted or parenthesized, with backslash-escaped delimiters, and no blank line inside. - Whitespace (spaces, tabs, at most one line ending) is allowed around the destination and title; destination and title must be separated by whitespace. - A link label has at most 999 characters and no unescaped brackets. No whitespace is allowed between link text and a following label or `()`. - Brackets inside link text must be balanced or backslash-escaped. Code spans, autolinks and raw HTML bind tighter than brackets. - Destination and title go through the shared unescape and entity helpers. The href is percent-encoded for non-ASCII and unsafe characters with the shared helper (an existing `%XX` stays as is), and the href and title are HTML-escaped. ## Reads - Inline text, the reference map. ## Writes - Link nodes in the inline tree. ## Programmatic Acceptance The Links corpus section includes image examples, so it is gated in the images story. The checks here are bounded. === AC links-inline-destination-and-title === Intent: An inline link renders one a element carrying the supplied destination, title and text. import subprocess text = "label" dest = "/uri" title = "the title" source = "[" + text + "](" + dest + ' "' + title + '")\n' result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("" + text + "") in result.stdout === END AC links-inline-destination-and-title === === AC links-reference-forms === Intent: Full, collapsed and shortcut references each resolve against a definition and render one a element. import subprocess definition = "\n\n[foo]: /url\n" for use in ("[text][foo]", "[foo][]", "[foo]"): result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input=use + definition, capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("` with ` title="..."` only when a title exists. The src is percent-encoded and HTML-escaped like a link href. - The alt value is the plain-text content of the description: emphasis, links and nested images are reduced to their text content (nested images contribute their own alt), code spans contribute their content, and the result is HTML-escaped. - `\![foo]` is a literal `!` followed by a link; `!\[foo]` is literal text. ## Reads - The inline tree built by the links story, the reference map. ## Writes - Image nodes in the inline tree. ## Programmatic Acceptance The Link reference definitions section is gated in the tabs story because its examples need headings and quotes. === AC images-corpus-sections === Intent: The Emphasis and strong emphasis, Links and Images conformance sections (roughly 240 cases) pass in full. The spaces or backslash are consumed. Leading spaces on the following line are dropped. - Any other line ending inside a block is a soft break, rendered as a line ending. Spaces at the end of the line and at the start of the next line are removed. - A hard-break marker at the end of a paragraph or heading is not a break: trailing spaces are dropped and a trailing backslash stays literal. - Breaks work inside emphasis and link text. ") == 1 assert first in result.stdout assert second in result.stdout === END AC breaks-hard-break-spaces === === AC breaks-hard-break-backslash === Intent: A backslash before a line ending gives one br element. import subprocess result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input="alpha\\\nbeta\n", capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("
") == 1 === END AC breaks-hard-break-backslash === === AC breaks-soft-break === Intent: A plain line ending is not a hard break and both lines stay in one paragraph. import subprocess result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input="alpha\nbeta\n", capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("
") == 0 assert result.stdout.count("

") == 1 === END AC breaks-soft-break === === AC breaks-none-at-block-end === Intent: Trailing spaces or a trailing backslash at the end of a paragraph do not create a break. import subprocess for source in ("alpha \n", "alpha\\\n"): result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("
") == 0 === END AC breaks-none-at-block-end === === AC breaks-inert-in-code-span === Intent: Trailing spaces before a line ending inside a code span do not create a break. import subprocess result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input="`code \nspan`\n", capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("
") == 0 assert result.stdout.count("") == 1 === END AC breaks-inert-in-code-span === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - A hard break must never occur at the end of a block. - Spaces in the middle of a text line must never be collapsed. - Do not skip, filter or reinterpret corpus examples. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Thematic-Breaks.md === # FEATURE: Thematic Breaks | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261014 V1 | | Description | Parse thematic breaks of three or more matching -, _ or * characters and render them as hr elements. | | Depends On | FEATURE-Line-Breaks-Text.md | | Provides | thematic break block | | Consumes | block-type registry | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Implement the Thematic breaks section of the spec as a registered block start rule. ## Rules - A thematic break is a line with up to three spaces of indentation, then three or more matching `-`, `_` or `*` characters, each optionally followed by any number of spaces or tabs. No other characters may appear on the line. - All non-space characters must be the same. Four or more spaces of indentation is not a thematic break. - A thematic break can interrupt a paragraph and needs no blank lines around it. - When a line could be a thematic break or a list item, the thematic break wins. When a line of dashes could be a thematic break or a setext underline, the setext heading wins; that wiring is added by the setext story. - It renders as `

`. ## Reads - Lines handed to the block engine. ## Writes - Thematic break nodes in the block tree. ## Programmatic Acceptance The corpus section needs lists, setext headings and emphasis, so it is gated in the lists story. The checks here are bounded. === AC thematic-three-markers === Intent: Lines of three or more matching marker characters each render one hr element. import subprocess lines = ["***", "---", "___", "_____________", " - - -", " ** * ** * ** * **"] source = "\n\n".join(lines) + "\n" result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("
") == len(lines) === END AC thematic-three-markers === === AC thematic-not-a-break === Intent: Wrong characters, too few characters, mixed characters and trailing text do not produce hr elements. import subprocess source = "+++\n\n--\n\n_ _ _ _ a\n\na------\n\n *-*\n" result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("
") == 0 === END AC thematic-not-a-break === === AC thematic-interrupts-paragraph === Intent: A thematic break directly after paragraph text splits it into two paragraphs around one hr. import subprocess result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input="Foo\n***\nbar\n", capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("
") == 1 assert result.stdout.count("

") == 2 === END AC thematic-interrupts-paragraph === === AC thematic-trailing-whitespace === Intent: Trailing spaces and tabs after the marker characters are allowed. import subprocess result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input="- - - - \t\n", capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("

") == 1 === END AC thematic-trailing-whitespace === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Mixed marker characters on one line must never form a thematic break. - Four spaces of indentation must never form a thematic break. - Do not skip, filter or reinterpret corpus examples. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-ATX-Headings.md === # FEATURE: ATX Headings | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261014 V1 | | Description | Parse ATX headings of levels 1 to 6 with optional closing sequences and render them as h1 to h6 elements. | | Depends On | FEATURE-Thematic-Breaks.md | | Provides | ATX heading block | | Consumes | block-type registry, inline parser hook | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Implement the ATX headings section of the spec as a registered block start rule whose content is parsed as inlines. ## Rules - An opening sequence of 1 to 6 `#` characters, preceded by up to three spaces of indentation, must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. Seven or more `#` is not a heading, and `#hashtag` is not a heading. - The content is stripped of leading and trailing spaces and tabs before inline parsing. - An optional closing sequence of `#` characters must be preceded by a space or tab and followed only by spaces or tabs. Backslash-escaped `#` characters are not part of the closing sequence. A `#` run followed by other text is content. - The heading level equals the number of opening `#` characters. A heading can be empty. - An ATX heading can interrupt a paragraph and needs no blank lines around it. - It renders as `content`. ## Reads - Lines handed to the block engine. ## Writes - Heading nodes in the block tree; inline content is parsed in phase 2. ## Programmatic Acceptance The corpus section uses indented code and thematic break interactions, so it is gated in the lists story. The checks here are bounded. === AC atx-levels-one-to-six === Intent: Each opening-sequence length from 1 to 6 renders exactly one heading of that level. import subprocess for level in range(1, 7): source = "#" * level + " foo\n" result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("") == 1 assert result.stdout.count("") == 3 === END AC atx-not-a-heading === === AC atx-closing-sequence === Intent: A closing hash sequence is removed from the heading content. import subprocess result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input="## foo ##\n", capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("

") == 1 assert result.stdout.count("#") == 0 === END AC atx-closing-sequence === === AC atx-empty-heading === Intent: Empty headings are allowed, one per line. import subprocess result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input="#\n\n##\n", capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("

") == 1 assert result.stdout.count("

") == 1 === END AC atx-empty-heading === === AC atx-interrupts-paragraph === Intent: A heading splits a paragraph without blank lines, leaving two paragraphs around it. import subprocess result = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input="Foo bar\n# baz\nBar foo\n", capture_output=True, text=True) print(result.stdout) assert result.returncode == 0 assert result.stdout.count("

") == 1 assert result.stdout.count("

") == 2 === END AC atx-interrupts-paragraph === === AC atx-indentation-limit === Intent: Up to three spaces of indentation are allowed before the opening sequence, and four are not. import subprocess allowed = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input=" # foo\n", capture_output=True, text=True) refused = subprocess.run(["./commonmark"], input=" # foo\n", capture_output=True, text=True) print(allowed.stdout) print(refused.stdout) assert allowed.returncode == 0 assert refused.returncode == 0 assert allowed.stdout.count("

") == 1 assert refused.stdout.count("

") == 0 === END AC atx-indentation-limit === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - A closing sequence must be preceded by whitespace; `foo#` keeps its hash. - Heading content must go through inline parsing, never be emitted raw. - Do not skip, filter or reinterpret corpus examples. === END ARTIFACT ===
